english.title: Remain on / enter premises in contravention of a Part 1A closure notice
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) remained on or entered into premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..) located at **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..) in contravention of a Part 1A closure notice issued by

(A)_[a police officer, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OFFICER WHO MUST BE OF THE RANK OF SUPERINTENDENT..),]_
(B)_[a local authority, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCAL AUTHORITY..),]_

under section 11A of the Anti-social behaviour Act 2003
english.legislation: Contrary to section 11D(1) and (3) of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003.

english.notes:
From 20th October 2014, the power to issue a closure notice under section 11A of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003 is no longer in force. The repeal does not, however, apply in relation to a notice issued before that date or anything done in connection with such a notice. As such, this offence can still be committed in relation to a notice issued before 20th October 2014.

Sections 11D(4) of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003 provides that a person who has a reasonable excuse for entering or being on the premises does not commit an offence.

other.penalty:
Summary: 51 Weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.Note:
In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference in subsection (3)(a) to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
